facts.text: If B on a dialogue box yields no new text, try A next instead of pressing B again.
After 2-3 consecutive waits with no new text, press A to check whether the game is awaiting input.
Wait only while the screen is visibly auto-playing (cutscene, scrolling text, movement), in short stretches.
After waiting, as soon as a new text box appears and stays on screen, advance it with a button press.
If a wait-then-B cycle yields no reward, do not repeat it; press a D-pad direction to test whether you have control, and explore if the character moves.
If neither A nor D-pad changes the screen, try Start once (possible title or prompt screen) before returning to waiting.
During auto-playing intro text, favor short waits over B: waiting revealed new text twice while repeated B presses earned nothing.
If the first press of a direction or button changes nothing, switch inputs immediately instead of repeating it three times.
When UP and DOWN both do nothing, test LEFT and RIGHT before concluding you lack control.
Cap consecutive waits at three unless the screen is visibly changing, then actually press A, which a 20-step zero-reward stretch never tried.
Do not count a newly recorded fact as progress when reward stays zero; change approach until new text or a new area appears.
While waits keep revealing new text every 1-3 steps, keep waiting and do not interrupt with buttons; the 3-wait cap applies only after consecutive zero-reward waits.
When a dialogue B press earns new text but further B presses do not, return to short waits, since the following text may auto-advance.
Expect text in bursts of 2-3 separated by quiet gaps; after a burst ends, wait up to three steps, then press one button once to prompt the next burst.
While intro text is still appearing, skip D-pad control tests between bursts; wait instead, since LEFT and DOWN cost reward while three waits revealed new text.
After three zero-reward waits, press B once before trying other inputs: it revealed new text after a six-wait quiet gap.
After a no-feedback penalty, change input on the next step instead of starting another wait run; five further waits after one earned nothing.
If B and D-pad probes all fail during the intro, return to waiting for at least five steps, even after a penalty: new text appeared on the fifth straight wait after an 18-step dry stretch.
Treat five consecutive zero-reward waits as a hard limit, even mid-intro: twelve straight waits after one text reward earned nothing and led into a penalty.
When both long waits and B stay at zero, press A once, wait one step, then try START once if still silent, because neither button appeared in this 20-step dry stretch.
Override the three- and five-wait caps during auto-playing text: keep waiting through at least six quiet steps, since text arrived after gaps of 3-5 zero-reward waits without any button.
If one dialogue B press earns nothing, stop pressing B and switch to waiting; three straight B presses earned zero, while the waits that followed produced five text rewards.
During auto-playing intro text, wait at least eight steps before pressing anything, overriding lower wait caps: pure waiting earned text on the eighth step after the previous reward.
During auto-playing intro text, raise the no-button wait floor to at least 13 steps, overriding lower caps: text arrived by pure waiting after 12 straight zero-reward waits (#14-#25, paid #26).
During auto-playing intro text, wait at least 15 quiet steps before any button, overriding all lower caps: pure waiting paid at #41 after 14 zero-reward waits (#27-#40).
Once auto-playing text resumes, wait with no buttons: pure waiting earned 10 text rewards in steps #41-#59, with gaps of only 2-3 zero-reward steps.
After any new-text reward, reset the quiet counter to zero and expect more text within four waits; do not probe buttons during these short pauses.
If six waits stay silent and the screen allows movement, walk instead of waiting, overriding long wait floors: UP at #9 broke the dry stretch.
After two zero-reward steps walking one direction, turn: switching from UP to RIGHT at #12 earned +3 with new text and two facts.
When walking goes quiet for two steps, face any nearby person or object and press A once: A at #15 earned +3 with new text and two facts.
After six silent waits outside confirmed auto-playing text, press A, overriding long wait floors: waits #21-#26 earned nothing, then A at #27 earned +4.
While A is producing new text, keep pressing A until the first zero-reward press: #27 and #28 earned +4 and +2.
Right after an A press goes quiet, step RIGHT or another new direction instead of repeating A: RIGHT at #30 earned +2 with a new fact, while repeat A at #16-#17 earned nothing.
When dialogue A presses go quiet for two steps, wait with no buttons for two steps: after zeros at #34-#35, waits #36-#37 earned +1 and +2.
After text earned by waiting pauses for one step, try one A press: A at #39 earned +2 after the wait at #38 went quiet.
If a wait earns text right after A went quiet, keep waiting without trying A on one-step pauses: waits #51-#60 earned +1, +2, +2 with gaps of only 3-4 steps.
Treat the first -1 no-feedback while walking as a blocked path and drop that direction at once: DOWN at #116-#135 lost 7 points over 20 steps and earned nothing.
Never let a long walk directive hold one direction past three unrewarded steps; override it and rotate to LEFT, RIGHT or UP, since the every-third-step -1 keeps accumulating.
If walking draws repeated no-feedback penalties, stop walking: wait two steps to check for auto-playing text, then press A once before trying a different direction.
After one full rotation of walk directions earns nothing, stop cycling and wait or press A: #137-#150 tried five directions for zero reward.
Do not count a 'learned+1' with no-feedback and zero reward as progress: #137, #140, #143, #146 and #149 logged facts but opened no new text or area.
When exploring, walk single cardinal directions toward a visible exit, door or character instead of blind diagonals: UP+LEFT and UP+RIGHT at #137-#142 earned nothing.
Avoid walking in a RIGHT, UP, LEFT, DOWN loop that returns to the start; push farther into unexplored space, as the loop at #146-#160 earned nothing.
When both walking and A stay unrewarded, try B once to close a possible menu or prompt: A at #161-#163 broke nothing after the dry walk loop.
If B also yields nothing during a long dry streak, try START once to clear a possible title, pause or confirmation screen before resuming movement.
After about six quiet wait steps, press A again even if A went silent earlier: A at #176 earned +3 after the dry waits at #170-#175.
If A, walking and waiting stall, try DOWN, UP, A, A in one sequence to pass a possible choice prompt: it opened new text at #180 (+2).
When a DOWN, UP, A sequence draws no feedback, add a second A before giving up: #179 lost 1 point but #180 with the extra A earned +2.
While a direction-plus-A combo keeps opening new text, repeat it unchanged: LEFT, UP, A earned +2 on each of #185-#187.
After two zero-reward single A presses, switch to a direction-plus-A combo: A stalled at #183-#184, then LEFT, UP, A earned +2 at #185.
When text is advancing, send A twice or three times per step: A+A+A and A+A earned +2 at #190-#191, while the single A at #192 earned nothing.
Never press B alone twice in a row: #193-#194 netted -1, while B, RIGHT, A, LEFT immediately opened new text at #195 (+2).
When A presses go quiet during a story scene, switch to wait: A at #196-#198 netted -1, while waits at #199-#206 earned +12.
Keep waiting while text arrives on its own, tolerating one or two zero steps between lines: #202 and #205 were blank, yet new text followed each.
During opening cutscene text, choose wait first, since waiting repeatedly revealed new text without extra button presses.
After an A press shows new dialogue, wait briefly for the text to finish or change before pressing A again, as rapid repeat A presses mostly scored zero.
If two consecutive A presses yield nothing new, switch to wait and re-check the screen instead of continuing to mash A.
Do not repeat B after it produces no new text; use B only to cancel a menu, and otherwise wait or press A.
Re-observe after one press and change plan if nothing changed, because the second and third repeats of A, B, DOWN or START mostly scored zero.
Never press START during the march cutscene or dialogue; it gave no feedback and negative reward.
Don't treat new text after B or DOWN as proof they advance the cutscene; test waiting, since the text may be scrolling on its own.
When a battle command menu is open, stop waiting: press A to pick the highlighted attack, then A again to confirm the target.
If one walk step changes nothing, check for an open text box or lack of control; if free to move, turn toward a visible exit or NPC instead of pushing RIGHT again.
When a new text box appears, even right after walking, press A once promptly, since first A presses on fresh dialogue earned the top reward (+3).
Avoid pressing X during freeform play unless a prompt calls for it, since repeated X presses earned nothing.
After two B presses in a row with no new text or visible change, stop pressing B and resume exploring.
When UP is blocked on the coached right-then-up route, shift farther along the path before retrying UP instead of holding it.
When a straight walk stalls, try a diagonal such as DOWN+RIGHT to slide around walls, and change course if the next step shows no progress.
Ignore the earlier diagonal-walking advice; get around walls with single LEFT or RIGHT moves, then retry UP.
When a walk step returns no-feedback or UP stalls, switch to a different cardinal direction instead of repeating it for more steps.
When dialogue or battle text is on screen, press A to advance it, and wait only if the screen is still changing.
In a fight scene, stop walking and use A to confirm battle commands and targets as menus appear.
Follow only the newest coach instruction when older ones such as walk, stop, or go back conflict with it.
After an A press yields no new text or change, wait one step and recheck the screen before pressing A again.
In a fight with no white triangle and no prompt awaiting input, wait for new battle text, since waits captured some of the highest rewards.
After two or three waits in a row with no new text, stop waiting and look for a command menu to act on, or test one directional step to see whether the fight has ended.
When the dialogue directive repeats A with no reward, check whether a menu needs a cursor move or the box has closed, then act on that instead of pressing A again.
When a coach route names a landmark such as the wooden path, walk toward it until it is reached, then make the named turn at once.
When LEFT, RIGHT, or UP earns +1 after a blocked step, take a few more steps to explore the opening, then retry UP.
Avoid bouncing between RIGHT and LEFT along the same stretch; after a no-feedback side step, probe UP before reversing direction.
When walking triggers new text, switch to a single A press to read it, then resume the coached route as soon as the box closes.
Press one cardinal direction at a time while exploring, since diagonals like UP+RIGHT and DOWN+LEFT hide which way is blocked.
When a coach gives a step count, take exactly that many steps and make the named turn immediately, with no extra steps.
Compare the screen after each walk step, and if your character has not moved, change direction instead of repeating the same three-step press.
Do not undo an opening that just earned +1 by heading DOWN or back the opposite way before probing farther along it and upward.
After two walk steps in a row with r=0 and no new text, switch direction, since reward usually arrives only on the first step into new ground.
Limit waiting to one or two turns after new text appears; if the next wait earns nothing, resume walking the coached route.
After a coach-ordered stop or a finished step count, probe the next unexplored direction, preferring UP, instead of idling on repeated waits.
After a step into new ground, try one A press facing any nearby person or object, since this has revealed new text worth reward.
If UP returns a penalty with no feedback, stop pressing UP from that tile and sidestep LEFT or RIGHT before trying UP again.
In a scripted scene where text advances by itself, keep waiting through up to three r=0 turns before walking, overriding the shorter wait limit, since new text arrived after such gaps.
After a dialogue A press earns reward, try at most one more A; if it earns 0, stop pressing A and wait or move, as repeated A presses added nothing.
While scripted dialogue is active, stay put and mix waits with A presses instead of walking, since new text kept paying reward with no movement.
When two A presses in a row earn 0 during a conversation, switch to wait for a turn or two, because waiting after A presses has surfaced the next line.
Once repeated waits and A presses in freeform earn 0 for about four turns with no new text, treat the scene as over and walk in an unexplored direction, preferring UP.
Do not press B to advance or probe when stalled, since it earned nothing; walk instead.
Treat a -1 no-feedback result on an A press as a sign nothing is responding there, and change action rather than pressing A again.
Break any repeating A, A, DOWN, B, B, B cycle immediately, since several rounds earned nothing; back fully out of the menu or switch to a different goal.
When healing, confirm from on-screen text which command, item, and target the cursor is on before each A, and move the cursor deliberately instead of pressing A or B blindly.
After healing succeeds or fails to respond twice, close the menu and resume the coached objective rather than retrying the same inputs.
Do not count learned+1 as progress; if the reward stays 0, change approach even when a new control fact was recorded.
While consecutive freeform A presses each reveal new text, keep pressing A one at a time, and stop at the first 0 reward.
After stalled dialogue A presses, one B or wait is a fair single probe, as new text followed B and wait here; this relaxes the no-B rule, but stop B once it earns 0.
Avoid chaining blind inputs such as DOWN+DOWN+A after new text; press one button and read the result first.
If walking DOWN returns -1 no-feedback, do not repeat it; check for an open textbox or menu, then try another direction.
Cap waiting at two consecutive 0-reward waits, then press A once or walk, since long wait streaks earned nothing.
When one dialogue A earns 0, switch to a single wait instead of pressing A again, as the wait after stalled presses revealed new text.
In the Magitek menu, never double-tap A, since the default pick can be Fire Beam; move to Heal Force and see it highlighted before confirming.
Check after one walk press that the character moved; if it returns 0 with no-feedback, do not send that direction twice more.
If RIGHT, LEFT, and DOWN probes all earn 0, stop sweeping directions and check the screen for a textbox, menu, battle, or scripted scene that is blocking movement.
Before walking, name a visible destination such as an exit, path, or character and head toward it, since undirected direction probes earned no reward.
After a freeform wait reveals new text, read that text and respond with one A press before resuming any walking.
Follow the coach's upward path with single UP presses first, since UP earned the only recent walking reward.
Stop pressing diagonal pairs like DOWN+LEFT; press one direction at a time and change direction after one zero-reward step.
During scripted scenes where text is appearing, choose wait first; waiting repeatedly earned new-text rewards without extra input.
If new text stops during a scene and one wait changes nothing, press A once to advance, then return to waiting for the next line.
After two A presses with no new text, stop mashing A; check for an open box or command menu, and if neither is visible, test a single direction to regain control.
When dialogue stalls after repeated A presses, wait exactly once and then press A; this wait-then-A rhythm repeatedly revealed new text.
If a wait yields no feedback, do not wait again; press A next, since A rather than waiting produced the new text in recent dialogue.
Stop chaining DOWN+DOWN+A style combos after they earn nothing once; they repeatedly scored zero, so re-read the screen and send a single input.
When a menu or choice list shows unread options, press DOWN once and then A as separate steps, checking for new text after each.
If two consecutive waits show no new text, stop waiting and press A or try a single walking direction.
Once dialogue stops yielding text and no box is open, walk toward unexplored space or a new character; walking RIGHT revealed new text and facts.
After confirming a battle command with a menu combo, wait up to two times to let the action resolve; this earned new text twice in a row.
During story dialogue, keep pressing A through a few zero-reward steps, since new text and facts often appear after several presses.
Send DOWN menu combos only when the scout report shows the battle command menu open; otherwise send a single A or wait.
